issues.claim: File f item 348's §9.5 part (BCR-V9-16, applied as written: plus and minus step the declaration's size by (band max − band min) ÷ 8) is applied nowhere. Base §9.5 *Authoring surfaces* (l.13431) still reads the count badge's 'plus and minus that re-run the dry run at one more or one fewer'. V09 §4.5's T5 row (l.1729) steps `sizeM2` by (band max − band min) ÷ 8 citing item 348. V10 cites §9.5 through BCR-V10-12. The canon routed item 348 to determinism only, so §7.1 got its `sizeM2` part (l.9367) and §9.5 got none. The base and V09 now give two rules for one control.
issues.required_change: Base §9.5 *Authoring surfaces*: replace 'with plus and minus that re-run the dry run at one more or one fewer' with BCR-V9-16's text: 'with plus and minus that re-run the dry run at the next step of the declaration's size — a quarter's `sizeM2` by (its band's maximum − its minimum) ÷ 8, clamped into the band, from the median when unset; a fill's density dial by one step (V09 §4.5); a roster's badge has none (its size is its lines)' (file f item 348).

issues.claim: V10 reads the calibration register from a file that never ships. V10 §1b.1 (l.254) reads 'each cell's calibration register entry from V12 §2.6's `register.json`'. §2.13's `RuleAnswer.register` (l.1018–1019) is `{ id; status; method; due }`, 'the cell's entry in V12 §2.6's plat/calibration/register.json'. V12 §2.10 (l.759–777) makes `dist/evidence.json` the one shipped copy that the clerk's `RuleAnswer` reads: it takes `entry`, `status` (with 'owner' for a stamped cell), `method` and `due`, and an absent or mismatched file shows the provenance source alone; `plat/calibration/` never ships. V09 §4.14 (l.344, l.2454) already reads `dist/evidence.json`. So the two readers of one record disagree, and V10 names a field (`id`) that the file does not have. V12's cross-part note 2 and the assembler's report flag the same.
issues.required_change: V10 §2.13: `register?: { entry: string; status: CalibrationEntry['status'] | 'owner'; method?: CalibrationEntry['method']; due?: string } /* the cell's row in V12 §2.10's dist/evidence.json, where one exists; an absent file or one of other table versions: the provenance source alone */`. V10 §1b.1 l.254: '… each cell's calibration record from V12 §2.10's `dist/evidence.json`'. Any 'details' text that names `id` names `entry`.

issues.claim:
The history store's device defaults (256 MB on the desktop tier, 96 MB on the low-end tier; 8 frames kept in memory) are stated nowhere in the set.
- Archive: V09 §5.12 stated them (inventory V09-0701, which the canon homes at V09 §5.12) and so did AppPrefs.history (V09-0151).
- Live V09 replaced them: §2.11 (l.892) has 'their defaults and ranges are V06 §2.2's' and §5.12 (l.3592) points to V06 §2.2.
- Live V06 §2.2 (l.570) and §6.5 (l.3585) point back to 'V09 §9', so the pointers form a loop.
- V06 §6.5's '≈ 150 CITY or ≈ 60 METROPOLIS epochs' now rests on an unstated size.
VV56-02 (blocker, owner V06) found the same loss but makes V06 §2.2 the home. The canon makes V09 the home: V09-0701 is a home at V09 §5.12, and V06-0100 is a reference to V09. The two fixes must agree on that one home.
issues.required_change: V09 §5.12's History line: 'History — history store memory (default 256 MB on the desktop tier, 96 MB on the low-end tier) and frames kept in memory (default 8); per-device, outside the recipe, the log and every digest (V06 §2.2 reads them)'. V09 §2.11 `AppPrefs.history`: `{ storeMB: number /* default 256 desktop, 96 low-end tier (V09 §5.12) */; frames: number /* default 8 */ }`, replacing 'their defaults and ranges are V06 §2.2's'. Resolve VV56-02 to the same home: V06 cites, V09 states.

issues.claim: V06 §2.2 (l.570) and §6.5 (l.3585) cite 'V09 §9' for the history store's device settings. V09 §9 is the decisions table. The settings are V09 §2.11 (`AppPrefs.history`) and §5.12 (the Settings dialog). V06 §6.5 (the home of V06-0319) also dropped its '256 MB desktop, 96 MB low-end' bound.
issues.required_change: V06 §2.2 and §6.5: cite 'V09 §5.12' (and V09 §2.11's `AppPrefs.history`) in place of 'V09 §9'. V06 §6.5 reads '≤ the device's setting (V09 §5.12: 256 MB desktop, 96 MB low-end)', the values V09 states under VV910-03.

issues.claim:
Item 119 (c)'s progress view reads a worker message the base never declares fully.
- V09 §4.21.9 (3) (l.3256–3258) and V09 §1b's row (l.354) say stage progress 'reaches the shell from the generation worker as each stage starts (the worker host's messages, §1.7's worker boundary; §12's progress rule), never polled', for every one-time wait in §4.21.9 (1).
- Base §11.2's `PlatApi` gives `generate` an `onProgress?: (p: Progress)` whose `Progress` type is declared nowhere (l.14265).
- `advance` has its own `{ epoch; of }` (l.14287).
- `open` (a migration, opening from SettlementForge), `regenerate`, `adjust` (Re-derive) and `export` have no progress option at all.
The hook is one-ended (V09's cross-part note 5). VRC0S-05 writes §12's progress rule but not this interface.
issues.required_change: Base §11.2: declare `type Progress = { stage: StageId; index: number; of: number } /* posted as each StageDecl starts */ | { wait: 'epoch'|'history'|'dossier'|'export'|'migrate'; done: number; of: number }`. Give `open`, `regenerate`, `adjust` and `export` the same `opts.onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void` that `generate` has. Make `advance`'s callback that `Progress` (`wait: 'epoch'`). §12's progress rule cites it.

issues.claim:
V09 places the worker boundary in base §1.7, which is the tech stack (§1.7 'Tech stack (reasons; …)'):
- §1b's progress-view row (l.354): '§1.7's boundary';
- §4.21.9 (3) (l.3257–3258): '§1.7's worker boundary'.
The worker boundary and its messages are §11.2 ('The embedding API and the worker boundary').
issues.required_change: V09 l.354 and l.3257–3258: replace '§1.7's boundary' and '§1.7's worker boundary' with '§11.2's worker boundary (`onProgress`)'.

issues.claim:
E-04 makes §7.1's binding table the one home that V09 §4.3 cites and T-V9-12 checks pair by pair (V09-ICONF-2). Two homes disagree with V09 §4.3 and V06 §4.2:
- (a) `setAttr` on `Enceinte.pathway` (a ring's fate: road, absorb or keep) is homed at T3 `wall` by V09 §4.3 (l.1620) and V06 §4.2 (l.3253). §7.1's T3 row (l.9752) does not name it, so the T9 catch-all ('every `setAttr` path no other row homes', l.9758) homes it at T9 `shape`.
- (b) `setAttr` on `WaterBody.spring.flow` (§2.3, item 111) is homed at T2 `ground` by V09 §4.3 (l.1615) and V06 §4.2 (l.3258). §7.1's T2 row (l.9751) names only `geology`, a bank class and a site feature, and a spring is not a `SiteFeature` (§2.3: hill, spur, valley, terrace, cliff, ravine), so it too falls to T9.
The other two mismatches in the same table, `wearWall` and `rerollLayer('forest')`, are already raised (VDC0-04; VDC0-15, VV78-13).
issues.required_change: Base §7.1's binding table: the T3 `wall` row adds '`setAttr` on `Enceinte.pathway`', and the T2 `ground` row adds '`setAttr` on `WaterBody.spring.flow`', so each has one home, matching V09 §4.3 and V06 §4.2.
